passages.text: Senecio glaucus is an annual member of the Asteraceae and species of the genus Senecio. It is found from the western Mediterranean to Central Asia in sandy, well-drained soil, particularly coastal and desert dunes.

Distribution and habitat
Found in sandy soils of coastal plains, strands, and steppes.

Native to the Palearctic
Middle East: Afghanistan, Algeria, Egypt - Sinai, Israel, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Syria, Tunisia, Turkey - Anatolia
Macaronesia: Canary Islands - Gran Canaria, Fuerteventura, Gomera, Hierro, Lanzarote, Tenerife
East Europe: Saratov Oblast, Volgograd Oblast, Astrakhan Oblast, Rostov Oblast, Kalmykiya
Southeastern Europe: Bulgaria, Crete, Crimea, Greece, Italy, Kosovo, Malta, Montenegro, Serbia, Sicily
Southwestern Europe: Balearic Islands, France, Portugal, Spain
Western Asia: Israel
Caucasus: Adygea, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Chechnya, Dagestan, Georgia, Ingushetia, Kabardino-Balkaria, Karachay–Cherkessia, Krasnodar Krai, North Ossetia–Alania, Stavropol Krai
Central Asia: Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan
India: Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir

Subspecies
Three subspecies are accepted.
Senecio glaucus subsp. coronopifolius {{small|(Maire) C.Alexander}} (synonyms S. chrysanthemifolius {{small|DC.}}, S. coronopifolius {{small|Desf.}}, S. desfontainei {{small|Druce}}, S. gallicus subsp. coronopifolius {{small|Maire}}, S. glaucus subsp. hyblaeus {{small|Brullo}}, S. lacerus {{small|Boiss.}}, S. laxiflorus {{small|Viv.}}, S. noeanus {{small|Rupr.}}) – Sicily, Malta, and Canary Islands to Sahara, western and Central Asia, Caucasus, and western Himalayas
Senecio glaucus subsp. cyprius {{small|Meikle}} – western and southwestern Cyprus
Senecio glaucus subsp. glaucus (synonym S. joppensis {{small|Dinsm.}}) – Egypt, Sinai, and the Levant
